features.title: Domain mutations and revision concurrency
features.summary: How canonical resources change: only through domain-specific atomic mutations under revision concurrency, shared by every transport through one application layer, with out-of-band edits detected and a retryable refusal when persistence is busy.
features.body:
## Sources

- Discussion #1 body (Part 1 consolidation, edited before the 2026-10-02+ amendments; later accepted comments win): Canonical Decision Index items 9 and 10; implementation-entry checklist step 2. https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/discussions/1

- Discussion #1 comment 165 (2026-09-30), "Accepted decision group — Preview/runtime architecture (A / A / A / A)": decision 4: `/api/*`, `/mcp` and `/preview/*` are separate transport adapters over one shared application layer; MCP never calls `/api/*` over loopback HTTP; transport routes do not duplicate domain logic. https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/discussions/1#discussioncomment-18671359
- Owner ruling 2026-10-07 (checkpoint B, item B2), recorded in PR #73 (https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/pull/73): the retryable `persistence.busy` refusal (HTTP 503 with `Retry-After`; MCP error result) on a persistence lock wait timeout is accepted; the `Retry-After` seconds value is not normative.
- code@c0a685e `src/persistence/busy.ts`: retryable `persistence.busy`. https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/blob/c0a685e72154d2fea1da811996de8484ebea25a0/src/persistence/busy.ts

- The `Retry-After` value (1 second, `PERSISTENCE_BUSY_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS` at c0a685e) is an implementation choice, not part of the specification (checkpoint B, item B2).

features.title: Evidence freshness
features.summary: Whether existing formal Evidence still validates a View is decided from structured change domains, so only affected captures need to be rerun while invalid or stale Evidence keeps blocking readiness.
